subject: Design review: VPC HSM transit lane & sealed-secret replication for private deploy
messages:
From: Roberto Alvarez <roberto@acme-corp.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.example.com>
Cc: ACME Infra Team <infra@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2025-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deploy: HSM transit lane + sealed-secret replication — kickoff

Diego,

Thanks again for taking the time. We've started scoping a private deployment in our VPC that must integrate our on-prem HSM pair (Thales) for BYOK, and we want to ensure the HSM transit path and secret replication model meet our compliance needs (FISMA/SOC2-like controls). High level asks:

- Confirm recommended network topology for a single-tenant VPC with an HSM transit lane and minimal egress footprint.
- Patterns for "sealed-secret" replication across availability zones so operator access is minimized during rotation.
- Operator procedures for key rotation and emergency unseal that don't expose key material over the public internet.

I've attached a rough network diagram and a one-page runbook outline. Can we do a design review early next week?

Roberto
Infra Lead, Acme Corp

Date: 2025-10-05T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: HSM transit lane + sealed-secret replication — kickoff

Roberto — thanks for the context and attachments. Looping in Kimberly (security lead) and Jordan (platform architect) to align on the review and to capture any platform constraints.

Quick note on scope: we should separate two concerns for the session so we can get practical decisions quickly:

1) Network & egress hardening for HSM transit lane (mutual TLS, peering/privatelink, firewall rules, route tables)
2) Secrets lifecycle & sealed-secret replication model (how secrets are wrapped by the HSM, where wrapped material lives, rotation handoffs, operatorless unseal patterns)

Proposed agenda for a 60-minute review: 10m kickoff & goals, 20m network topology & connectivity options, 20m KMS/HSM integration patterns + rotation, 10m decisions & next steps.

Kimberly/Jordan: any immediate redlines we should add to the agenda?

— Diego
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.example.com>, Roberto Alvarez <roberto@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2025-10-06T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: HSM transit lane + sealed-secret replication — kickoff

Thanks Diego, Roberto. A few operational constraints and initial recommendations to seed the design review so we make concrete decisions during the meeting: 

Top-level constraints (Acme told us in intake): no inbound public IPs on control plane; HSM must be in customer-controlled network, keys never leave HSM in plaintext. Audit evidence required for every rotation.

My recommendations (high level):
- Connectivity: prefer VPC-Peering with route table restrictions plus a dedicated Transit Subnet containing the Redwood KMS proxy instances. If the customer prefers managed connectivity, use Privatelink/NVA pair — but confirm latency to HSM is within KMS SLA.

- Mutual attestation: enforce mTLS with client certs issued by Acme's CA. HSM-side connector (on-prem gateway) should verify Redwood proxy cert and vice-versa. Certificate rotation documented in runbook.

- Sealed-secret model: wrap secrets inside HSM (wrap_token = HSM.wrap(plaintext_key)). Store only wrapped blobs in Redwood's persistent store. For AZ replication, replicate wrapped blobs only (no unwrapped key material). Replica sync must be over the private transit lane and use HMACed manifests to detect tampering.

- Rotation & emergency unseal: prefer split-escrow for unseal keys (3-of-5 threshold) held by Acme witnesses. Redwood can provide an operatorless unseal flow that uses HSM-wrapped rekey-tokens for automated rotation without exposing raw keys to platform engineers.

- Egress minimization: outbound connectivity from the KMS proxy instances should be whitelisted to only Acme endpoints and Redwood monitoring endpoints via a controlled bastion; disallow general internet egress from the transit subnet.

Pre-meeting asks for Roberto:
1) Which PKI do you want us to use for mutual TLS (Acme CA, or a cross-signed intermediate)?
2) Can you provide the expected HSM latency numbers (RTT) and any firewall/ACLs that will sit between HSM and Redwood proxies?

I'll bring a draft set of runbook snippets for rotation and an evidence checklist (audit fields we will emit).

Kimberly Park
Security & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Roberto Alvarez <roberto@acme-corp.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.example.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>
Cc: ACME Infra Team <infra@acme-corp.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2025-10-06T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: HSM transit lane + sealed-secret replication — kickoff

Appreciate the quick recommendations. A few answers and clarifications: 

- PKI: we'll use our internal CA and can stand up a cross-signed intermediate for Redwood during the pilot.
- Latency: typical RTT to our on-prem HSM cluster is ~6–12ms from the transit point; throughput is modest (hundreds of ops/minute).
- ACLs: we have firewall rules that only allow specific subnets to reach the HSM gateway; we will provide an allowlist prior to the cutover.

Two additional asks: 
1) Can Redwood show an example audit event that proves a rotation occurred and which key handle was rotated? We need the field names for ingestion into our SIEM.
2) For sealed-secret replication, we want a demonstration of a cross-AZ failover where the new AZ can unseal without operator intervention (using Redwood's orchestrated rewrap flow).

I've attached an updated runbook outline with our internal ACLs and a proposed rehearsal date.

Roberto
[attachment: acme-runbook-outline-v2.pdf (PDF, 60KB)]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.example.com>
To: Roberto Alvarez <roberto@acme-corp.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2025-10-07T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: HSM transit lane + sealed-secret replication — kickoff

Thanks — solid answers, Roberto. Summary of agreed decisions and immediate next steps (to capture for the meeting notes and the pilot runbook):

Decisions: 
- Connectivity: start with VPC peering + transit subnet for the pilot. Move to Privatelink only if peering introduces unacceptable latency.
- PKI: Acme internal CA with a cross-signed intermediate for Redwood proxies.
- Sealed-secret storage: only HSM-wrapped blobs will be persisted in Redwood stores. Replication will use HMACed manifests over the transit lane.
- Rotation: automated rewrap flow using HSM-wrapped rotation tokens; Acme retains the unwrapping threshold via split-escrow witnesses. Redwood will emit rotation audit events compatible with SIEM.
- Egress: egress from transit subnet locked to Acme endpoints + specific Redwood telemetry endpoints; no general internet egress.

Action items (owners & target dates):
- Acme (Roberto): share allowlist CIDRs and sample firewall rules by 2025-10-10. (Roberto)
- Redwood (Diego): produce a stubbed audit-event spec (fields + example JSON) and attach to the runbook. Deliver by 2025-10-09. (Diego)
- Redwood (Kimberly): publish draft rotation runbook snippets and evidence checklist. Deliver by 2025-10-09. (Kimberly)
- Joint: schedule a rehearsal (cross-AZ failover) for week of 2025-10-20; confirm windows. (All)

I'll attach the updated meeting agenda and a link to a stub workspace showing the audit event schema for early review. If that looks good, we'll confirm the rehearsal date.

— Diego
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
